name: 7 Steps to a Business Model — Reinvent Atelier Lumière
description: A five-round, advanced business-model design simulation set inside Atelier Lumiere SAS, a regional French print house in Lille (founded 2009, peaked in 2017 at EUR 9.8M and 70 staff, now down to EUR 5.4M revenue, a 4% operating margin and 38 employees). Print revenue is falling ~12% a year and gross margin has compressed from 34% to 22% as clients commoditise the work. On Thursday 11 June 2026 the lead bank cuts the overdraft from EUR 600k to EUR 200k; the board issues an ultimatum - present a credible reinvented business model at the 9 July board meeting or prepare the company for sale. You play the Founder & CEO with EUR 1.8M of runway and eight years of design files, brand assets and content for ~600 regional SMEs. Built on Denis Dauchy's seven-step discipline, v2 scores the FIT BETWEEN decisions rather than each decision on its own: you commit to one of three strategies through the value proposition - a managed service, a self-serve platform, or a premium craft niche - and every later choice is judged against that commitment. All three can win and none is right in isolation: front-loaded cash modelling is correct for project revenue and fatal for recurring revenue, keeping the EUR 95k/month plant is correct for the craft strategy and fatal for the platform, and the right level of investment runs from EUR 80k to EUR 700k depending on the model chosen. The realistic conversion of the 600-client base is hidden: in round 1 you decide whether to buy research into a number you will not need until round 3, before you know which strategy you will pick. The plant bills every round until it is resolved, retaining the two senior designers costs EUR 120k of runway, and pitching a coherent model you have not actually built loses the board's confidence. Runs in English, Spanish and French. Final KPIs track Business-Model Coherence, Investor Confidence, Cash Runway in EUR, and the pivot Budget committed against the EUR 700k cap.

Atelier Lumière SAS · Lille, France · Board meeting 9 July 2026 — reinvent the model or sell the company

7 Steps to a Business Model

A regional print house is dying — print revenue is falling 12% a year and the bank has just cut the overdraft. You are the founder with €1.8M of runway, ~600 SME clients and eight years of their content. Using Dauchy's 7-step discipline, redesign the value proposition, choose a monetization logic, and make the operation cohere — before the cash runs out and the board sells the company.

Your Decisions This Step

You are paying now for a number you will not need until the monetization step — and before you know which model you will choose.
Committed up front: 450k of €700k
Drawn from the €1.8M runway. What the right number is depends entirely on the model you chose.
Conversion your revenue case assumes: 27%
Committed margin: 14%
Different models earn different margins. Claiming one you cannot reach costs more than claiming a modest one.
Conviction: 70
Lead seed investor & the board
You have eight years of content for 600 SMEs who are panicking about their digital presence — that is the raw material of a new business. But I will block a plan that bolts digital onto a print P&L without a real change in operating logic. Diagnose why print is dying before you redesign, anchor the value proposition in the customer's job and not your printing press, choose a monetization logic that survives the cash trough, and make the operation cohere with the promise — all inside the €1.8M you actually have.
